introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2021. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (code 0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A (Pure Mathematics, compulsory) and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B (Mechanics) or SECTION C (Statistics and Probability). In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. If Section B is chosen, Section C may not be chosen, and the other way round. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Electronic calculators may be used. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2. Formulae booklets may be used.

Le systeme ne sait exprimer que « 2 parmi 3 » par section ; l'exclusivite B ou C est recopiee dans introduction_markdown mais n'est pas appliquee par les regles_choix.

Points : le sujet imprime des points par sous-question, pas de total par question. Le champ points de chaque exercice est la somme des points imprimes des sous-questions (Section A : 8 ou 9 ; Sections B et C : 17, ce qui est coherent avec « all questions carry equal marks »).

Q9(iii) : le sujet ne precise pas le sens des mouvements ; lecture retenue : meme sens (S rattrape T), seule lecture coherente avec une vitesse de S de 6 m/s apres le choc et un T plus rapide (10 m/s).

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(a) A particle moves from rest in a straight line from a fixed point $O$, and after $t$ seconds of its motion, the displacement from $O$ is $x=(t^3+4t^2+6)$ m. Find the velocity of the particle when $t=2$. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Velocity is the derivative of displacement:

$v=\dfrac{dx}{dt}=3t^2+8t.$

At $t=2$: $v=3(4)+8(2)=12+16=28$.

**$v=28\ \text{m s}^{-1}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(b) Find the acceleration of the particle when $t=2$. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Acceleration is the derivative of velocity:

$a=\dfrac{dv}{dt}=6t+8.$

At $t=2$: $a=6(2)+8=20$.

**$a=20\ \text{m s}^{-2}$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(a) A particle $P$, of mass $3\,\text{kg}$ lies at rest on a smooth plane, inclined at $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. Given that the particle $P$ is attached to an inelastic string which passes over a smooth fixed pulley at the top of the plane, to another particle $Q$ of mass $6\,\text{kg}$ hanging freely, and that the system is released from rest with the string taut, find the common acceleration of the particles. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Let $T$ be the tension and $a$ the common acceleration ($Q$ moves down, $P$ moves up the plane). Take $g=10$.

For $Q$ (down is positive): $6g-T=6a$, that is $60-T=6a$. (1)

For $P$ (up the plane is positive, smooth plane): $T-3g\sin30^\circ=3a$, that is $T-15=3a$. (2)

Add (1) and (2): $60-15=9a\Rightarrow a=\dfrac{45}{9}=5$.

**$a=5\ \text{m s}^{-2}$.**
themes: connected particles on an inclined plane

questions.enonce_markdown: (iii)(a) Two particles $S$ and $T$ of masses $2\,\text{kg}$ and $3\,\text{kg}$ respectively are moving in a straight line with velocities $12\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ and $6\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ respectively. $S$ collides with $T$ and after the collision $S$ moves with a velocity of $6\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. Find the velocity of $T$ after the collision. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The particles move in the same direction (S catches up with T). Let $v$ be the velocity of $T$ after the collision. By the **conservation of momentum**:

$2(12)+3(6)=2(6)+3v$

$24+18=12+3v\Rightarrow3v=30\Rightarrow v=10$.

**$T$ moves with velocity $10\ \text{m s}^{-1}$** in the same direction as before.

questions.enonce_markdown: (iii)(b) Find the loss in kinetic energy after the collision. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Kinetic energy before: $\tfrac12(2)(12)^2+\tfrac12(3)(6)^2=144+54=198\ \text{J}$.

Kinetic energy after: $\tfrac12(2)(6)^2+\tfrac12(3)(10)^2=36+150=186\ \text{J}$.

Loss $=198-186=12$.

**Loss in kinetic energy $=12\ \text{J}$.**
